title: Uniform provisions concerning: I. Approval of specific equipment of vehicles of category M and N using liquefied petroleum gases in their propulsion system; II. Approval of vehicles of category M and N fitted with specific equipment for the use of liquefied petroleum gases in their propulsion system with regard to the installation of such equipment (version 4.2.0)
scope_summary: Part I approves the LPG 'specific equipment' as separate components, including containers, container accessories, vaporizers/regulators, valves, hoses, filling units, injectors, sensors, pumps, ECUs, gas tubes and multi-components. Part II approves vehicles of categories M and N1 that are fitted with such equipment, with regard to how it is installed.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to: 1.1 Part I Approval of specific equipment of vehicles of category M and N1 using liquefied petroleum gases in their propulsion system; 1.2 Part II Approval of vehicles of category M and N1 fitted with specific equipment for the use of liquefied petroleum gases in their propulsion system with regard to the installation of such equipment.
applies_to_components: Remotely controlled service valve with excess flow valve
Gas injection device / injector / gas mixing piece
Non-seamless and seamless gas tubes and their couplings
Gas tubes of materials other than copper, stainless steel and coated steel, and their couplings
Installation of the LPG system in the vehicle (Part II)
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories M and N1 as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.3.
Part II (vehicle installation) relies on components approved under Part I of the same Regulation.
Annex 14 requires the electronic control unit to comply with the relevant electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements. This in practice points to UN R10.
It refers to EN 589:1993 for automotive LPG fuel specification, and to ISO 188 and ASTM standards in the test annexes.
Interconnected LPG-systems have hydraulic interconnections with the petrol or diesel fuelling system.
Related in practice to UN R115 (retrofit LPG systems), which relies on R67-approved components. This Regulation's text does not state that relationship.

defined_terms.label: Component class
defined_terms.definition: High pressure parts including tubes and fittings containing liquid LPG with a pressure > 3,000 kPa.

defined_terms.label: Component class
defined_terms.definition: High pressure parts including tubes and fittings containing liquid LPG at vapour pressure or increased vapour pressure up to 3,000 kPa.

defined_terms.label: Component class
defined_terms.definition: Low pressure parts containing vaporized LPG with a maximum operating pressure below 450 kPa and over 20 kPa above atmospheric pressure.

defined_terms.label: Component class
defined_terms.definition: Low pressure parts for a limited pressure range containing vaporized LPG with a maximum operating pressure below 120 kPa and over 20 kPa above atmospheric pressure.

defined_terms.label: Component class
defined_terms.definition: Shut-off valves and pressure relief valves, when operating in the liquid phase.

defined_terms.label: Pressure
defined_terms.definition: The maximum pressure to which the component is designed to be subjected and on the basis of which its strength is determined.

defined_terms.label: Pressure
defined_terms.definition: The maximum allowable operating pressure in a component according to its classification.

defined_terms.label: Product scope
defined_terms.definition: The list of LPG components (a) to (t), from container through gas tubes of other materials, that can be approved under Part I.

defined_terms.label: Component

defined_terms.label: Container variant
defined_terms.definition: A container with a cylindrical shell, two dished ends either torispherical or elliptical and the required openings.

defined_terms.definition: Containers other than standard cylindrical containers, with dimensional characteristics given in Annex 10, Appendix 5.

defined_terms.label: Container variant
defined_terms.definition: A container made only of composite materials with a non-metallic liner.

defined_terms.label: Type
defined_terms.definition: Containers not differing in trade name, shape, openings, material, welding process, heat treatment, production line, nominal wall thickness, diameter and height.

defined_terms.label: Component group
defined_terms.definition: 80% stop valve, level indicator, pressure relief valve, remotely controlled service valve with excess flow valve, fuel pump, multivalve, gas-tight housing, power supply bushing, non-return valve and pressure relief device, either separate or combined.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device that limits the filling at maximum 80 per cent of the capacity of the container.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to verify the level of liquid in the container.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to limit the pressure build-up in the container.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device aimed to protect the container from burst in case of fire by venting the LPG contained.

defined_terms.term: Remotely controlled service valve with excess flow valve
defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: An ECU-controlled device that establishes and interrupts LPG supply to the evaporator/pressure regulator, closed when the engine is not running, with an excess flow valve limiting LPG flow.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to establish the supply of liquid LPG to the engine by increasing the pressure of the container with the fuel pump supply pressure.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device consisting of all or part of the 80% stop valve, level indicator, pressure relief valve and power supply bushing.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to protect the accessories and to vent any leakages to the open air.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: Electrical feed-through for fuel pump/actuators/fuel level sensor.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to allow the flow of liquid LPG in one direction and to prevent the flow in the opposite direction.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device intended to vaporize LPG from a liquid to a gaseous state.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device intended for reducing and regulating the pressure of liquefied petroleum gas.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to cut off the flow of LPG.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to prevent the pressure build-up in the tubes above a pre-set value.

defined_terms.term: Gas injection device or injector or gas mixing piece
defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device which establishes the liquid or vaporized LPG to enter the engine.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device which meters and/or distributes the gas flow to the engine, either combined with the gas injection device or separate.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device which controls the LPG demand of the engine and automatically cuts power to the LPG shut-off valves in case of a broken fuel supply pipe caused by an accident, or by stalling of the engine.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device which measures pressure or temperature.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device which filters the LPG; the filter can be integrated in other components.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: Hoses for conveying LPG in either a liquid or vapour state at various pressures from one point to another.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: An assembly of a flexible hose and couplings.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A device to allow filling of the container, either integrated in the 80% stop valve or as a remote filling unit at the outside of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A coupling in the fuel line between the fuel container and the engine, allowing a monofuel vehicle that is out of fuel to run from a service fuel container.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: A pipe or duct that connects the fuel injection devices.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: Any of the specific components combined or fitted together as a component.

defined_terms.label: Component
defined_terms.definition: Tubing made of metallic material, designed not to flex in normal operation, through which LPG flows.

defined_terms.label: Fuel
defined_terms.definition: Any product essentially composed of propane, propene, normal butane, isobutane, isobutylene, butene and ethane.

defined_terms.label: System
defined_terms.definition: A set of LPG specific equipment intended to be fitted in a vehicle to constitute an integrated and functional whole enabling propulsion with LPG.

defined_terms.label: System
defined_terms.definition: An LPG-system having hydraulic interconnections with the petrol or diesel fuelling system.

applicability_hints: Any part containing LPG at more than 20 kPa above atmospheric falls under a class (0, 1, 2, 2A or 3). Parts designed for below 20 kPa are not subject to the Regulation.
One component may contain several parts, each classified separately according to its pressure and function.
Combined or integrated assemblies are approvable as a 'multi-component' or 'multivalve'. Filters integrated in other components still count as LPG filter units.
The LPG ECU is specific equipment and must also meet EMC requirements (Annex 14). ECUs for interconnected systems have additional provisions.
Electrical items in contact with LPG, such as power supply bushings, actuators and level sensors, are covered. So are electrically operated valves, with insulation rules in 6.17.2.
Fuel pumps mounted inside the container change the container marking ('PUMP INSIDE') and their design-temperature range.
Gas tubes, including non-copper or non-steel materials and their couplings, are approvable specific equipment.
Liquid-injection or interconnected systems sharing hydraulics with petrol or diesel fuel systems trigger the ICS provisions (17.13, Annex 16 9.7).
Non-metallic parts carry extra marking (manufacturing month/year) and material tests: ozone, creep, temperature cycling and LPG compatibility.
A vehicle approval (Part II) covers the installation, LPG identification sticker, ventilation and gas-tight housing. Components must be Part I approved.
Remote filling units mounted on the vehicle exterior are covered as filling units, including the J15/K15/Euro heavy-duty connector impact tests.
